what_happened: Registering W07-01 required appending two obligation entries into checkpoint.json's
open_obligations_before_next_card array. That array holds 203 mixed entries (dicts and strings)
and the file does not round-trip under json.dumps, so the edit had to be text surgery. My insert
expression was ',' + join('\n' + indent + element) - a single leading comma for the whole batch -
so the two new entries landed with NO comma between them and checkpoint.json became invalid JSON
(Expecting ',' delimiter at the second inserted line) for roughly two minutes.
how_it_was_repaired: A textual insert of the missing comma at the exact break, guarded by asserts (the R3 marker
occurs exactly once, the character before the newline is a closing quote, the next non-space text
begins with the R4 marker), followed by json.loads on the whole file and a re-check that revision
140, expected_previous_revision 139 and current_step_id null survived. No restore, no checkout, no
reset: nothing that any other writer had done was discarded, and my own intended edits were kept.
blast_radius: The broken bytes were never committed - the freeze commit 743bb1ec touched only receipts/W07/W07-01,
and the checkpoint's last valid committed state is rev 139 in e745f624. task_packet.py was not run
against the broken file before the repair, so no registration decision was made on it.
rule_this_teaches: A batch insert needs a separator PER element, not one leading comma. The 旧例 guard for shared
append points (assert the key is absent, prove a no-op re-dump reproduces the bytes, compare the
untouched remainder) passed here precisely because it refuses to write what it cannot re-parse -
the abort happened at the verification read, after both files were on disk, which is the one window
the existing guards did not cover. Any future array append must parse the candidate text BEFORE
disclosure_why_it_matters: A concurrent reviewer measures whatever is on disk. Had w0701_verifier_r1 still been
running it would have read an unparseable checkpoint, and an unattributed failure would have looked
like a product defect. This file exists so the sequence is reconstructable rather than silently
